messages.text: I'm interested in the Bitfortun BS-1 model (5.1TH/s) but I missed the offer. Will it be available in distribution, and if so, when?

The B.1 is off sale right now while BitFortun fixes a firmware issue, and there's no date set for it coming back. I can put you on the notify list for it.

Meanwhile, the Hammer BC04 is 6 TH/s at $239, in stock and shipping now. Want me to compare the two?
Searched the catalog · Hammer Miner BC04 6 TH/s

Straight comparison: the BS-1 is 5.1 TH/s at $229 and you can't buy it today. The B.04 is 6 TH/s at $249, ~100W, ~50 dB, WiFi or ethernet, in stock and shipping in 2–5 business days. So slightly more hashrate, same class of machine, and it's actually on the shelf.

At ~100W it's about 72 kWh a month — roughly $7 at 10¢/kWh. What do you pay per kWh, and is this your first miner?
This is not my first one, I have a Bitaxe GAMMA 601 and a few NerdMiner V2

Then you're already in the lottery game — a 6 TH/s BC04 is about 5x your Gamma, but the Thor P2 at $369 gives you 10 TH/s for ~166W and it's quieter (~40 dB), also in stock. Better per TH than the BS-1 ever was.

What's your power rate, and does noise matter where these sit?
In your opinion, do they work better over wifi or LAN ?

LAN, every time. Wired keeps the stratum connection stable, so you lose fewer shares to dropouts and reconnects — hashrate is the same either way, uptime isn't. 2.4 GHz WiFi in a room with a few miners gets flaky.

Both the BC04 and Thor P2 have ethernet. Your Gamma and NerdMiners are WiFi-only, so that's a real upgrade.
I think so too, I'm looking and wondering about the version with a LAN port, currently my budget is set at a max of $250

Then the BC04 is your unit: $249, 6 TH/s, ethernet port, ~100W, in stock and shipping in 2–5 business days. It fits the budget with a dollar to spare and it's the cheapest wired miner we have.

Want me to build the cart so you can check out?
